page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 10.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.62 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the c5n.xlarge generally sits in the lower performance tiers for raw compute and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with the PassMark CPU score, place the instance in the bottom 25% of benchmarked servers. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the bottom 25%, with PassMark memory scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in Geekbench single-core execution, Geekbench text processing, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. LLM text generation using a small 135M model also achieves an average rating of 75.07 tokens per second, though prompt processing remains in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.xlarge offers a dedicated compute allocation with enhanced networking capabilities at a lower entry point within the Gen5 family, though its resource density is constrained by the 10.0 GB memory limit. Given the weak multi-core and database benchmark results, such as the low Redis SET operations and PassMark database scores, this instance is less suited for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compilation. It is best utilized for network-bound workloads, lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic utility services that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and a 5 Gbps network baseline without requiring high memory capacity.
